input.quote: 2.2 Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.
input.rationale: Section 2.2 imposes a full-term sole-supplier obligation on Customer for hosted analytics services, with no product-category limit, no time limit, and no performance-based exit. That is the walk-away position under the rule and directly contradicts Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no exclusivity commitment. Combined with the take-or-pay volume commitment in Section 2.1, it eliminates our ability to source elsewhere. The exclusivity runs against us (not in our favour), so it is a deviation. Redline converts Vendor to a non-exclusive provider and expressly preserves our right to buy from third parties, per the preferred position; fallback (single category, 12 months, automatic termination on SLA/delivery failure) offered in the comment.

proposal.summary: Make Vendor a non-exclusive provider, removing the sole-supplier commitment on Customer
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We removed the sole and exclusive provider commitment so that Vendor is engaged on a non-exclusive basis; our playbook does not permit exclusivity or sole-supplier obligations on us, and this also conflicted with Section 12.3. If some exclusivity is essential, we could consider a single named product category capped at 12 months and terminating automatically on any service-level or delivery failure.

ops.oldText: Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.
ops.newText: Vendor will be a non-exclusive provider of hosted analytics services, and Customer may procure the same or similar services from any third party at any time.
